AshNicolus opened PR #99: fix: join anonymous interior nodes across path segments instead of cross-joining
Closes #95

A path like (a)-[:R]->()-[:S]->(c) gets lowered into two independent edge segments. Each segment lowers its own copy of the shared interior node, and since a bare () has no identifier, both copies got binding: None. The executor joins segments by shared binding name, so two unrelated Nones share nothing and it fell back to a full cross join, matching every S edge in the graph against every R neighbor of a. A DELETE or SET on that pattern mutated vertices the path never reached.

lower_row_patterns now gives an anonymous interior node a synthetic binding shared by both segments that meet there, so the existing name-based join sees they must be the same vertex. Named interior nodes are untouched: the synthetic name is only used as a fallback when the AST has no real identifier. The label/property validation that already rejects an anonymous node carrying labels or non-id properties still checks the real identifier, not the synthetic one, so that restriction is unchanged.

The synthetic name is filtered back out of collect_row_node_bindings so WITH's pass-through validation still sees only the bindings the query text actually wrote.
